heroHeadline: Russian Banderol Missiles Kill 10 in Kharkiv Region as Ukraine Launches 620-Drone Barrage on Moscow
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,637 (August 18, 2026), Russia struck the village of Pechenihy in Kharkiv region with Banderol jet-powered cruise missiles, killing 10 people and wounding 18+ at a residential intersection lined with homes, a cafe, and a post office; a further 5 were wounded in nearby Izyum. The strike came amid a 147-drone overnight barrage that also hit Brovary in Kyiv region. Hours later, Ukraine launched one of its largest drone assaults of the war — more than 620 drones targeting Moscow region — striking the Wildberries logistics warehouse for a second time in days along with sites in Pavlovsky Posad, Orekhovo-Zuyevo, and Kolomna; Moscow's mayor reported 180 drones downed over the oblast, and Russian state media TASS called it the largest such attack on the capital in two years. The prior day (August 17) saw a Russian drone strike kill 2 civilians at a Zaporizhzhia gardening community, while Ukrainian rockets struck Koloskovo village in Russia's Belgorod region, killing 6. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached ~1,469,970 by August 18, per the Ukrainian General Staff.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Euronews, PBS NewsHour, GlobalSecurity.org, United24 Media, Wikipedia War Timeline, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
